olivia.sales: Heads-up — MediPortal POC requests Dedicated endpoints in two regions (us-west, eu-west) and wants to allowlist by IPv6 + IPv4. They also asked whether POC traffic counts toward a Reserved commit and if we can provide per-region egress IPs.

ryan.platform: Short answer: we can provision per-region Dedicated pools and assign stable IPv4 egress addresses per pool. We do NOT currently publish native IPv6 egress for Dedicated pools (hosted). Hosted API supports IPv6 hostname resolution, but Dedicated static egress IPs are IPv4-only today.

kevin.netops: Workarounds for IPv6-only customers:
- Recommend they NAT64 on their side to reach our IPv4 egress.
- Or front the call with a customer-side proxy that speaks IPv6 and NATs to our IPv4 allowlist.
Both options avoid changing our infra. If they're insisting on dual-stack from our side, that's an engineering project with lead time.

olivia.sales: Got it. They specifically asked for sample firewall lines for both regions and a quick verification command for ops. Can we paste a copy/paste snippet?

kevin.netops: Paste below — replace with assigned IPs once pool is provisioned. Also included a curl verification using IPv4 forced mode.

```
# Allowlist entries (replace with provided IPs)
# US-WEST Dedicated pool
203.0.114.10/32   # redwood-dedicated-usw-egress

# EU-WEST Dedicated pool
203.0.114.11/32   # redwood-dedicated-euw-egress

# Example iptables rule (if self-managing outgoing allowlist)
# Allow outbound TCP/443 to Redwood dedicated egress (USW)
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 203.0.114.10 --dport 443 -m comment --comment "allow redwood-usw" -j ACCEPT

# Basic smoke test (force IPv4 so IPv6-only hosts still test mapping)
curl -4 -sS -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDFLOW_POC_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://dedicated-usw.redwood.ai/v1/healthz
```

kevin.netops: If they need an IPv6 verification step (to validate their NAT64/proxy path), they can run a curl to their proxy endpoint or use `curl -6 --resolve` against an internal proxy that maps to our IPv4. We'll provide guidance during the handoff call.

sasha.sec: Security notes for questionnaire: Dedicated pools enforce TLS 1.2+; we log request metadata and can provide per-request traces in Console for the POC. Client certs (mTLS) require Private/VPC deployments and CA exchange. If they insist on client cert authentication for hosted Dedicated, we can evaluate a limited custom arrangement but it needs legal signoff.

megan.solutions: On billing/commit: standard approach is one of three options: (A) POC is charged normally and counts toward commit; (B) we exclude POC usage from counting if sales/legal sign a POC addendum; (C) provide credits equal to X hours of dedicated capacity. For speed, we usually propose option B with explicit dates (POC start/end) so their finance team is comfortable.

olivia.sales: Thanks — they also asked about IP rotation policy (how often do our dedicated IPs change?).

sasha.sec: Egress IPs for a given Dedicated pool are stable for the life of the pool. We only change them for maintenance/security incidents; non-emergency rotations get at least 48h notice, emergency changes are communicated ASAP.

megan.solutions: Action items: (1) Sales to confirm POC dates + infra contact and whether they can NAT to IPv4; (2) Platform to provision two pools and return assigned IPs; (3) Solutions/legal to prepare POC addendum option B if customer wants exclusion from Reserved commit.

infra-bot: [provisioning] dedicated-pool/prod-mediaportal-euw created by @ryan.platform — pool-id p-d4e5f6euw — egress: 203.0.114.11

olivia.sales: Awesome, I'll send the allowlist snippet and schedule a 30m handoff. I'll also ask whether they want the POC excluded from their commit and attach the addendum draft. Thanks all! :white_check_mark:
